items.title: 68189_Al Hall oral history interview
items.q: Beethoven (Inaudible) hasn't changed since he's given what he did

ctx.x: Cliques, you know. It's a political ballgame. And then you get the seniority bit. If you've never been there, you never get any seniority. But out of the thousands of musicians that there are, there are very few Black musicians that are working in any phase of it, except jazz, and that's looked down upon government-wise, as far as funding goes. They give millions to the symphony orchestras.

Beethoven (Inaudible) hasn't changed since he's given what he did, but Luther Anderson changed his support. Fred Norman was a guy -- Fred Norman's been around as long as I can remember trying to get a job as an arranger, and he's one of the finest arrangers there is.

You have to be brash or flaky, you know, to gain attention. You can't just be Al Hall, you know. You got to be something else to get attention. You can't take anything for granted. You got to be in there pitching all the time, to make sure that you get your piece of the action.
